spans.s:
Nakha denotes either the ‘nail’ of a man, or the ‘claw’ of a wild beast, such as a tiger. The trimming (nikṛntana) of the nails was a regular part of the toilet of the Vedic Indian, especially on occasions of special sanctity, when it accompanied the cleansing of the teeth.
Foot notes Rv. i. 162, 9; x. 163, 5; Av. ii. 33, 6, etc.
Rv. iv. 3, 3. Cf. x. 28, 10, of the eagle's talon.
Chāndogya upaniṣad, vi. 1, 6.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 5, 1, 7; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 6, 2, etc.; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, ii. 1, 3, 4.
